=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 244-260 (scope-resolution block after the `elif security_audit_flag_enabled "${SECURITY_AUDIT_INCREMENTAL}"` branch)
  Problem: When `git cat-file -e` or `git merge-base --is-ancestor` fails inside the incremental-enabled branch, `CHANGED_FILE_COUNT` is never assigned because that variable is set only inside the `if git cat-file && git merge-base; then` block. The `elif [ "${CHANGED_FILE_COUNT}" -gt "${SECURITY_AUDIT_INCREMENTAL_MAX_FILES}" ]` and `else` clauses at lines 256-259 are chained off that same `if git cat-file` and will execute when the git checks fail. With CHANGED_FILE_COUNT unset, `[ "" -gt 200 ]` evaluates false, so the `else` branch runs and sets `AUDIT_SCOPE_MODE="incremental"` with an empty `CHANGED_FILES_FILE`. The audit then runs against zero changed files and the post-filter drops every finding.
  Why it fails at runtime: On a shallow clone or history rewrite where the last-audited commit is unreachable, the script silently produces zero findings instead of falling back to a full audit. With `fetch-depth: 0` in the workflow this is unlikely in CI, but the code defect is real and would trigger in any environment where `git cat-file` or `git merge-base` fails against the tracker-recorded SHA.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: line 261 (`else` clause of the inner `if [ SHA == HEAD ]`)
  Problem: When `LAST_AUDITED_SHA` is non-empty but `SECURITY_AUDIT_INCREMENTAL` is disabled, the script falls into this `else` and reports `"last audited commit ${LAST_AUDITED_SHA} is missing or not an ancestor of HEAD (history rewrite?); falling back to a full audit"`. The message is wrong: the branch fires because the operator disabled incremental scanning, not because the commit is missing or rewritten.
  Why it fails at runtime: The behavior is correct (falls back to full scope), but the log message misdirects operators to investigate a nonexistent history-rewrite problem instead of the actual reason (INCREMENTAL disabled).
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: The PR introduces `scripts/workflow_retro_fanout.sh` as a new script referenced in README.md:1171 and agents.md:572. The repo CI lint (`tests/inventory_parity.py`) enforces that every script referenced in README.md and agents.md is registered in `docs/INVENTORY.md`.
  Expected change site: docs/INVENTORY.md — Scripts section needs an entry for `scripts/workflow_retro_fanout.sh`.
  Evidence of absence: `grep -c "scripts/workflow_retro_fanout" docs/INVENTORY.md` returns 0. The sibling script `scripts/workflow_retro.py` is registered. Running `python3 tests/inventory_parity.py` produces three linked failures: `FAIL: docs/INVENTORY.md: Scripts: missing scripts/workflow_retro_fanout.sh`, `FAIL: README.md:1171: references scripts/workflow_retro_fanout.sh but docs/INVENTORY.md does not document it`, `FAIL: agents.md:572: references scripts/workflow_retro_fanout.sh but docs/INVENTORY.md does not document it`.

- File: scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 852-858
  Problem: The grep command for changed file count lacks the -c flag in the count branch: `grep . "$CHANGED_FILES_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true` outputs line content, not count. The variable CHANGED_FILE_COUNT expects a numeric value for arithmetic comparison at line 855: `[ "$RESULT" -gt "$SECURITY_AUDIT_INCREMENTAL_MAX_FILES" ]`, but grep without -c produces the actual matching lines, breaking integer comparison logic.
  Why it fails at runtime: When files exist in CHANGED_FILES_FILE, the expansion produces non-numeric text (file paths), causing bash arithmetic evaluation to fail with "integer expression expected". When no files exist, the count command yields empty string instead of 0, causing same arithmetic failure or incorrect logic flow.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
